### Also covered by

Fong & Spivak, *Seven Sketches in Compositionality*, §7.2.1 (printed p. 225; PDF p. 237; item `7sketches:7.2.1:remark-topos-properties`) opens the topos section with the same five-item list of Set-like properties this issue's Awodey source states, asserted without proof: a topos has all limits, has all colimits, is cartesian closed, has epi-mono factorizations, and has a subobject classifier. The colimits clause is this issue's obligation and Seven Sketches adds nothing to it.

Two of the other clauses are handled elsewhere in the Seven Sketches catalog rather than here: clause (iv), the epi-mono factorization in a topos, is filed as its own issue for Seven Sketches §7.2.1 (together with the uniqueness of the factorization in `Sets`), and the remark's corollary "since Set is a topos, all five hold for Set" belongs to #404 — Phase-D verification confirmed there is **no `ElementaryTopos Sets` instance in the tree at all**, `Instance/Sets/Classifier.v` deliberately carrying cross-universe theorems instead, so `Instance/FinSet/Topos.v:38`'s `FinSet_Topos` is the library's sole assembled topos.

One clause of the list is neither in this issue's scope nor filed anywhere, and it is a real obligation: clause (i), "a topos has all limits". `Structure/Topos.v:112`'s `ElementaryTopos` carries finite-limit data as terminal object + binary products + pullbacks, and the file header discloses that the reduction of pullbacks to products and equalizers is deliberately not formalized — so there is no finite-completeness theorem for a topos and no equalizer field.

- [ ] (from Seven Sketches §7.2.1) An elementary topos is finitely complete: derive equalizers from products and pullbacks and state finite completeness as a theorem about `ElementaryTopos`, closing the reduction that `Structure/Topos.v`'s header records as not formalized.

### Also covered by

Fong & Spivak, *Seven Sketches in Compositionality*, §7.2.1, Definition 7.5 (printed p. 226; PDF p. 238; item `7sketches:7.2.1:def7.5`) *defines* a monomorphism to be a morphism `f : A → B` for which the square with both legs out of the apex equal to `id_A` and both legs into `B` equal to `f` is a pullback — i.e. it takes this issue's characterization as the definition rather than deriving it from cancellation. So the obligation is the same one, seen from the other side.

Phase-D verification of the Seven Sketches record confirmed the in-tree situation is exactly as this issue describes: `Theory/Morphisms.v:116` `Monic` is the cancellation form (with `Epic` at `:104` and the `C^op` duality recorded in their own comments at `:102` and `:114`), and no lemma anywhere relates `Monic f` to the square being a pullback — a search for `Monic.*IsPullback`, `monic_iff` and friends turns up only `Structure/Abelian.v:170` `monic_iff_kernel_pzero` (an additive zero-morphism test) and `Instance/FinSet/Classifier.v:335` `finset_monic_iff_injective`.

One trap worth recording, because it is the nearest-looking in-tree statement and is *not* this one: `Theory/Subobject/Functor.v:127` states `IsPullback id m y m id` — identity horizontals with `m` on both verticals — and it holds for **every** `m`, monic or not. The square this issue needs has `id` on both legs out of the apex and `f` on both legs in.

The dual half of Definition 7.5 (an epimorphism as a pushout square) is recorded on #323.

### Also covered by

Fong & Spivak, *Seven Sketches in Compositionality*, §7.2.1, Definition 7.5 (printed p. 226; PDF p. 238; item `7sketches:7.2.1:def7.5`) *defines* an epimorphism to be a morphism `f : A → B` for which the square with corners `A, B, B, B` and legs `f, f, id_B, id_B` is a pushout — the cokernel-pair characterization this issue owns, taken as the definition. Seven Sketches adds no hypotheses; it states the mono and epi cases together as one definition, and the mono half is recorded on #672.

Phase-D verification confirmed the gap is exactly as this issue states: `Theory/Morphisms.v:104` `Epic` is the cancellation form, and nothing in the tree relates it to the pushout square. `Structure/Regular.v:46`'s `kernel_pair f := pullback f f` is the dual construction on the other side and is never identified with the diagonal precisely when `f` is monic, which is the corresponding fact for #672.

### Also covered by

Fong & Spivak, *Seven Sketches in Compositionality*, §7.2.2 (printed p. 229; PDF p. 241; item `7sketches:7.2.2:construction-subobject-classifier-set`) builds the same object in running prose: `Ω_Set` is the two-element boolean set with `true : 1 → Ω`, the characteristic function of an injection `m : X ↣ Y` sends `y` to true exactly when `y` lies in the image of `m` (display (7.14)), and conversely a predicate `p : Y → Ω` classifies `{y ∈ Y | p(y) = true}` (display (7.15)) — exhibiting the bijection between subsets of `Y` and functions `Y → Ω`.

Phase-D verification added a constraint this issue should absorb before work starts, because it decides where the theorem can live. The library **deliberately does not** build a `SubobjectClassifier Sets` instance: `Instance/Sets/Classifier.v`'s header (lines 12–77) states the one-universe-level obstruction itself and declines to claim the folklore no-go as a theorem, and what it supplies instead is cross-universe *theorems* over `PropSetoid` (carrier `Type@{o}` under `iffT`, `:151`) — `sets_char_pullback` at `:224`, `sets_char_unique` at `:283`, `sets_char_subobject` at `:341`, all stated in `Sets@{so sso}`. The char rule there, `char_setoid m b := ∃ a, m a ≈ b` (`:186`), *is* the book's image-membership rule, but its truth values live one universe up and are not a two-element set. The only single-level instance of the book's construction in the tree is skeletal: `Instance/FinSet/Classifier.v:353` `FinSet_Classifier` with `Ω := 2%nat`, `truth := fun _ => fin_true` and `char := fin_of_bool (fin_existsb …)`, both obligations closed by `Qed` (`:361`, `:392`), together with `finset_monic_iff_injective` at `:335`. Nothing in the tree connects the two — there is no "the inclusion of `FinSet` into `Sets` preserves the classifier" statement.

- [ ] (from Seven Sketches §7.2.2) The concrete bijection of display (7.15) — subobjects of `Y` correspond to maps `Y → Ω` — stated and proved at a level where `Ω` really is the two-element set, i.e. for `FinSet`, and related to the cross-universe `Sets` theorems so the two accounts are visibly one story rather than two disconnected ones.

### Also covered by

Fong & Spivak, *Seven Sketches in Compositionality*, §7.3 (printed pp. 231–232; PDF p. 244; item `7sketches:7.3:remark-presheaf-topos`) asserts the same theorem without proof: any small category `C` may be regarded as a site, and the corresponding topos is the functor category of presheaves `C^op → Set` — in particular the category of database instances on a schema is a topos, and such toposes are called presheaf toposes.

The site half of that remark (making "presheaves count as sheaves" precise via a trivial coverage) is not restated here; it is scheduled with this chapter's §7.4 topos-as-sheaves issue, which owns the trivial coverage and the equivalence `Sheaves(C, trivial) ≃ [C^op, Sets]`.

Phase-D verification sharpened the in-tree inventory for this issue in a way worth recording: of the five topos ingredients for a functor category, exactly one is proved — `Instance/Fun/Cartesian.v:111` `Functor_Category_Cartesian` gives pointwise products. `ls Instance/Fun/` contains `Cartesian.v` and nothing else, so there is no `Closed`, `Terminal` or `HasPullbacks` instance for `@Fun` anywhere, no classifier, and `sieve` occurs only twice in the tree, both prose. The library never over-claims here: `Instance/Fun.v:59-66` attributes "cartesian closed / free cocompletion" to nLab and then separately states what is in-tree.

- [ ] (from Seven Sketches §7.3, footnote 5) The covariant functor category `C ⟶ Set` is also a topos, obtained by using `C^op` as the site — the dual half of the remark, which the presheaf statement alone does not give.

### Also covered by

Fong & Spivak, *Seven Sketches in Compositionality*, §7.3.1, Example 7.23 (printed p. 233; PDF p. 245; item `7sketches:7.3.1:example7.23`) states the same identification: the arrow shape has two objects and two non-identity morphisms `src, tgt : Vertex → Arrow`, and a presheaf on it is exactly a directed graph, with a worked instance drawn (display (7.24)).

Phase-D verification confirmed both in-tree endpoints and, importantly, that they are not connected. `Instance/Parallel.v:80` `Parallel` **is** the book's arrow shape (two objects, exactly two non-identity arrows `ParX ⇒ ParY`), its header at `:152-161` states the graph reading in prose, and `Instance/Parallel.v:166` `Presheaf_Graph : Parallel^op ⟶ Sets` is one specific graph-as-presheaf with hard-coded `nat` vertices and `nat * nat` edges — the variance is right, since in `Parallel^op` the maps go `ParY → ParX` so `fmap` sends an edge to its endpoints. On the other side, `Construction/Free/Quiver.v:358` `QuiverCategory` is the category of graphs, but `Class Quiver` at `:54` makes edges a **dependent family** `edges : nodes → nodes → uedges`, not a `(G₀, G₁, src, tgt)` triple. So the re-encoding is real work: a search across the seventeen files mentioning `Parallel` finds no functor or equivalence bridging to `Quiver`.

The example's closing slogan — presheaves on `C` are the free colimit completion of `C` — is recorded on #346.

append_block:
### Also covered by

Fong & Spivak, *Seven Sketches in Compositionality*, §7.3.1, Example 7.23 (printed p. 233; PDF p. 245; item `7sketches:7.3.1:example7.23`) closes with the unproved slogan that the category of presheaves on `C` is the free colimit completion of `C` — the same content this issue owns from the density side, stated by Seven Sketches as motivation for reading presheaves as "lego constructions glued out of the shapes of `C`".

Phase-D verification confirmed the slogan is unformalized in-tree by any route: a search for `cocompletion`, `free colimit` and `colimit completion` returns exactly three hits, all prose — `Instance/Fun.v:63`, `Theory/Sheaf.v:117` and `Construction/Day.v:111` — with no theorem behind any of them.

The graph half of the example (presheaves on the arrow shape are directed graphs) is recorded on #705.

### Also covered by

Fong & Spivak, *Seven Sketches in Compositionality*, §7.3.2, Definition 7.25 (printed p. 234; PDF p. 246; item `7sketches:7.3.2:def7.25`) gives the same definitions this issue schedules: a topology on a set `X` is a family of subsets containing `X`, closed under binary intersection and under arbitrary unions (the empty union giving that `∅` is open); a topological space is a set with a topology; and a continuous function is one whose preimages of opens are open.

Phase-D verification independently reproduced the whole negative: `topological space`, `open set`, `open subset`, `opens of`, `OpenSets`/`Opens`/`open_sets` and `Definition Top`/`Category Top`/`Instance Top` all return **zero** hits across the tree, and every one of the twenty-three files matching `topolog` is prose or bibliography. Every `continuous` hit is the limit-preservation sense (`Adjunction/Continuity.v`, `Structure/Limit/Preservation.v`). The one structure that looks adjacent was examined and correctly rejected: `Theory/Sheaf.v:159` `Class Site` is a coverage on an *arbitrary* category, with no underlying set, no opens and no continuous maps — and it has no instance anywhere in the tree.

Seven Sketches adds one piece of vocabulary to this issue's definition list, and the rest of its Chapter 7 depends on it: the notion of a **cover**. Definition 7.25 says that when `U` is the union of a family `(Uᵢ)` of opens, the family *covers* `U`; that is the input to the sheaf condition of §7.3.3 and to every covering-family argument in §7.4.

- [ ] (from Seven Sketches §7.3.2) The covering relation on a topological space — a family of opens whose union is `U` covers `U` — defined alongside the topology, with the empty family covering `∅` as an instance.

### Also covered by

Fong & Spivak, *Seven Sketches in Compositionality*, §7.3.2, Example 7.28 (printed p. 235; PDF p. 247; item `7sketches:7.3.2:example7.28`) names the two extreme topologies on any set — the coarsest `{∅, X}` and the finest `P(X)` — and calls `(X, P(X))` the discrete space. These are exactly the two topologies produced by the left and right adjoints of the underlying-set functor that this issue builds, so no new general theorem is demanded; the DoD of this issue already has to construct both in order to have the adjoints.

Phase-D verification recorded the corresponding negatives, all reproducible: `coarsest` returns zero hits, `finest` returns exactly three and all concern the finest *congruence* on a setoid quotient (`Instance/Sets/Coend.v:26,72`, `Instance/Sets/Pushout.v:26`), `powerset` returns zero, and `indiscrete` returns only `Structure/Discrete.v:24`, which is about the `Cat`-level indiscrete right adjoint and not a topology. `Instance/Discrete.v:37`'s `DiscreteCat` is the discrete *category* on a type (homs are equality proofs) and must not be mistaken for the discrete space.

### Also covered by

Fong & Spivak, *Seven Sketches in Compositionality*, §7.3.2, Exercise 7.29 (printed p. 235; PDF p. 247; item `7sketches:7.3.2:ex7.29`) asks for the verification that the two extreme families really are topologies, and then for the fact that every function out of a discrete space is continuous. Both fall inside this issue's existing scope: the verifications are what constructing the left and right adjoints requires, and "every function out of a discrete space is continuous" is precisely the transpose of the discrete-topology adjunction — that is, it is the universal property the adjoint already has to satisfy, not an added obligation. No checkbox is added for that reason.

Phase-D verification recorded one negative worth keeping in the file: `continuous` in the preimage-of-open sense returns **zero** hits tree-wide, and `discrete topology` returns zero. The nearest in-tree neighbour is `Instance/Discrete.v:52` `DiscreteCat_Functor {A : Type} {C : Category} (f : A → C) : DiscreteCat A ⟶ C`, whose file header at `:29-32` describes it as "the left adjoint `Set ⟶ Cat` at the level of a single functor" — i.e. the adjunction itself is not built there either. That is the `Cat` analogue of this issue's `Top` statement and may be a useful template.

### Also covered by

Fong & Spivak, *Seven Sketches in Compositionality*, §7.3.2, Exercise 7.32 (printed p. 236; PDF p. 248; item `7sketches:7.3.2:ex7.32`) gives the same construction this issue owns: for `Y ⊆ X`, a subset `A ⊆ Y` is open in the subspace topology exactly when `A = B ∩ Y` for some open `B` of `X`. Its three parts — exhibit a `B` witnessing that `Y` itself is open, verify the subspace topology satisfies the three topology axioms, and show the inclusion `Y → X` is continuous — are all inside this issue's existing scope, since the subspace topology cannot be exhibited as a sliced adjoint inverse without them. No checkbox is added for that reason.

Phase-D verification confirmed the negatives: `subspace` returns **zero** hits tree-wide and `continuous` returns only the limit-preservation sense. Two near-misses were examined and rejected, and both rejections are worth carrying: `Construction/Subcategory.v:31` `Record Subcategory` selects objects and morphisms of an ambient *category* and has no induced-structure content; and `Instance/Ens.v:56` `EnsT T` has homs `∃ f : T → T, ∀ x, In A x ↔ In B (f x)` — membership preservation *and* reflection along a function — so it is neither the inclusion order nor the continuity condition.

### Also covered by

Fong & Spivak, *Seven Sketches in Compositionality*, §7.3.2 (printed p. 236; PDF p. 248; item `7sketches:7.3.2:construction-opens-preorder`) builds the same object in running prose: inclusion makes the opens of a space a preorder (reflexive since `U ⊆ U`, transitive since `U ⊆ V ⊆ W` gives `U ⊆ W`), and via the preorder-as-category passage this yields a category `Op` whose objects are the opens and whose hom-set `Op(U,V)` is empty when `U ⊄ V` and a singleton when `U ⊆ V`. Seven Sketches adds the role, not the construction: this category is the **site** over which its presheaves and sheaves are then defined, and the sheaf development that consumes it is scheduled as this chapter's §7.3.3 issue.

Phase-D verification confirmed the split precisely. The generic passage is present and exact: `Instance/Proset.v:33` is `Program Definition Proset {A : Type} {R : relation A} (P : PreOrder R) : Category` with `hom := R` and `homset equiv := fun _ _ => True`, i.e. the trivial hom-setoid that realizes thinness, with `id` from reflexivity and `compose` from transitivity; `Instance/Poset.v` adds antisymmetry. What is missing is any instantiation at an inclusion order — `Proset` is never applied to one — and the opens themselves. Two further candidates were checked and rejected: `Instance/Props.v:39` (propositions under implication) and `Instance/Ens.v:56` `EnsT T`, whose homs are preimage-style *functions*, not inclusions, so `EnsT` cannot supply `(Op, ⊆)`. The only analogous reflexivity/transitivity facts in the tree are `Theory/Subobject.v:62`/`:67` `sub_le_refl`/`sub_le_trans` for subobjects (both closed with `Defined.`, so they are Type-level data).

### Also covered by

Fong & Spivak, *Seven Sketches in Compositionality*, §7.4.2, display (7.56) (printed p. 245; PDF p. 257; item `7sketches:7.4.2:eq7.56`) fixes the meet and join half of the same Heyting structure this issue owns: for opens `U, V` of a space, conjunction is `U ∩ V` and disjunction is `U ∪ V`. In Seven Sketches these are the truth values of a sheaf topos, which is why the identification matters there, but the mathematical obligation — the open-set lattice with its meets and joins — is this issue's.

Phase-D verification recorded the in-tree position: the only Heyting-flavoured structure in the tree is on Coq's `Prop` (`Instance/Props.v:69` `Props_Cartesian` with `product_obj := and`, `:80` `Props_Cocartesian` with `product_obj := or`, `:94` `Props_Closed` with `exponent_obj := Basics.impl`), the file states that reading explicitly at `:15-27`, and **nothing links it to the truth-value object of a topos**. A search for `Heyting` returns exactly seven hits and all seven are comments (`Theory/Sheaf.v:85`, `Instance/Props.v:15/17/27`, `Theory/Lawvere.v:87`, `Instance/Two.v:86`, `Structure/Topos.v:81`) — there is no Heyting-algebra class at all.

### Also covered by

Fong & Spivak, *Seven Sketches in Compositionality*, §7.4.2, display (7.57) (printed p. 245; PDF p. 257; item `7sketches:7.4.2:eq7.57`) gives the implication of this issue's open-set Heyting algebra by its explicit formula: `U ⇒ V` is the union of all opens `R` with `R ∩ U ⊆ V`, equivalently the largest such open. The surrounding prose stresses that this is the connective that admits no further reduction.

Phase-D verification pinned down why the in-tree material does not cover it, and the distinction is the reason this remains an obligation: what exists is only the *abstract characterization* of implication as a right adjoint to meet — `Structure/Cartesian/Closed.v:51` `exp_iso {x y z} : x × y ~> z ≊ x ~> z^y`, instantiated at one concrete posetal model in `Instance/Props.v:94` (`exponent_obj := Basics.impl`) — i.e. class **data**, whereas the book's `U ⇒ V := ⋃{R : R ∩ U ⊆ V}` is a **construction by arbitrary joins**. The library has no frame or locale and no arbitrary joins in a poset, so the construction cannot be carried out today; this issue's complete-lattice setting is where it belongs.

### Also covered by

Fong & Spivak, *Seven Sketches in Compositionality*, §7.4.2 (printed p. 245; PDF p. 257; item `7sketches:7.4.2:def-negation`) defines negation in the open-set Heyting algebra as `¬U := (U ⇒ ⊥)`, unwinds it to the union of all opens disjoint from `U`, and observes that a reader who knows topology will recognise this as the **interior of the complement** of `U` — which is exactly why intuitionistic negation on opens is not complementation.

Phase-D verification examined and rejected the two in-tree near-misses, and both rejections should survive into the work. First, `Structure/Monoidal/StarAutonomous.v`'s `dual`/`double_dual` is **linear** negation over a symmetric monoidal closed base with the dualizing isomorphism axiomatised — the opposite of Heyting negation, and citing it would be a same-name-weaker error. Second, `Instance/Props.v` does make `¬P` *expressible* as `exponent_obj P False` (`Props_Initial` at `:61`, `Props_Closed` at `:94`), but no such definition or lemma is ever written. The tree's only zero-exponential facts are `x^0 ≅ 1` (`Structure/BiCCC.v:236`) and `prod_zero_l`/`prod_zero_r`; there is **no** lemma about `0^x`, which is what negation would be.

- [ ] (from Seven Sketches §7.4.2) `¬U` on the open-set lattice identified with the interior of the complement of `U`, connecting this issue's Heyting negation to the interior operator of #727.

### Also covered by

Fong & Spivak, *Seven Sketches in Compositionality*, §7.4.2, Exercise 7.60 (printed p. 246; PDF p. 258; item `7sketches:7.4.2:ex7.60`) asks for the top and bottom of this issue's open-set Heyting algebra together with their laws: the whole space `X` behaves as true (`X ∧ U = U`, `X ∨ U = X`, `U ⇒ X = X`, `X ⇒ U = U`) and `∅` behaves as false (`∅ ∨ U = U`, `∅ ∧ U = ∅`, `∅ ⇒ U = X`).

Phase-D verification checked every in-tree analogue individually and all six line numbers are exact: `Structure/Cartesian.v:451` `prod_one_l` (`1 × x ≅ x`), `Structure/Cocartesian.v:375` `coprod_zero_l` (`0 + x ≅ x`), `Structure/BiCCC.v:208` `prod_zero_l` (`0 × x ≅ 0`), `:236` `exp_zero` (`x^0 ≅ 1`), `Structure/Cartesian/Closed.v:389` `exp_one` (`x^1 ≅ x`) and `:415` `one_exp` (`1^x ≅ 1`) — so six of the seven clauses have a generic counterpart about a terminal `1` and an initial `0`.

The seventh does not, and it is not a bookkeeping omission: the clause `⊤ ∨ U = ⊤` (generically `1 + x ≅ 1`) is nowhere proved and is **not derivable** in a general bicartesian closed category — it needs posetality. Phase D also corrected a claim in the coverage record here: thin categories *do* exist in-tree as instances (`Instance/Proset.v`, `Instance/Poset.v`, `Instance/Props.v`, `Instance/Two.v`); what is missing is a thin/posetal *class* and any absorption law stated over it.

- [ ] (from Seven Sketches §7.4.2, Exercise 7.60) The absorption law `⊤ ∨ U = ⊤` proved for the open-set lattice — the one clause of the exercise with no generic bicartesian-closed counterpart, since it holds only in the posetal setting.

### Also covered by

Fong & Spivak, *Seven Sketches in Compositionality*, §7.4.2, Example 7.58 (printed p. 246; PDF p. 258; item `7sketches:7.4.2:example7.58`) works this issue's open-set Heyting algebra out on a concrete pair: on the real line with its usual topology, for `U = (−∞, 3)` and `V = (−4, 4)`, it computes the conjunction `(−4, 3)`, the disjunction `(−∞, 4)`, `¬U = (3, ∞)`, `¬V = (−∞,−4) ∪ (4,∞)`, `U ⇒ V = (−4, ∞)` and `V ⇒ U = U`. It is the worked check that intuitionistic negation on opens is not classical complementation — the same point this issue makes as "the failure of the Boolean laws", here with numbers.

Phase-D verification re-ran the decisive negative: `Coq.Reals`, `Rdefinitions` and `R_scope` return **zero** hits over all `.v` files — the real numbers are not imported anywhere in the library — so this computation has no possible in-tree home today, and whichever issue lands the open-set lattice must decide the numeric substrate.

- [ ] (from Seven Sketches §7.4.2, Example 7.58) A worked computation of all six connective values on two concrete opens of the real line, as the numeric witness that negation on opens is not complementation.

### Also covered by

Fong & Spivak, *Seven Sketches in Compositionality*, §7.4.2, Exercise 7.59 (printed p. 246; PDF p. 258; item `7sketches:7.4.2:ex7.59`) supplies the sharpest concrete witness for this issue's "failure of the Boolean laws" clause: on the real line take `U` to be the complement of the origin; then `¬U = ∅`, `¬¬U` is the whole line, `U ⊆ ¬¬U` holds and the reverse inclusion fails. One direction holds in every Heyting algebra and the other fails here — which is the whole content of the failure.

Phase-D verification recorded the near-miss it deliberately did **not** count as coverage, and the reasoning is worth keeping: `Structure/Monoidal/StarAutonomous.v`'s `star_double_dual` *axiomatises* `x ≅ ¬¬x`, i.e. precisely the law this exercise exhibits as failing, so citing it would have been a same-name-weaker error. Independently confirmed: no reals, no topology, no Heyting negation, and zero hits for `double negation` anywhere in `.v` files.

- [ ] (from Seven Sketches §7.4.2, Exercise 7.59) The punctured-line witness: `U ⊆ ¬¬U` proved and `¬¬U ⊆ U` refuted for a named open, exhibiting the failure of double-negation elimination concretely rather than as a general remark.
